lines.en: I had it in a safe place, and then I moved it to protect it,
Then she left a string of clues.
A minimal, unhelpful note, these appear to be human teeth,
It's a movie, but I've never seen it.
It's, like, about lame werewolves and vampires and stuff.
Dollars to donuts, this points us her way.
Finally, a scavenger hunt worthy of my time.
We have a wonderfully small number of clues.
Did you see this movie about vampires and such?
Yeah, I saw it with April.
She was so hopped up on painkillers from getting her wisdom teeth out,
I convinced her to see it with me.
You were super out of it.
You kept yelling, "Team Voldemort!" at the screen,
You only get to see the second "Twilight" film for the seventh time once.
Do you remember anything about a key?
Or April doing anything unusual that day?
She did make a stop by the shoeshine stand before we left
because she wanted to drop something off for Andy.
She had a real bad crush on him.
Oh, babe, you had a crush on me.
Or maybe it was never here.
They must have moved it during the remodel.
And we definitely do not live down here now.
Guys, where's the old shoeshine stand from upstairs?
We don't know anything about that.
We are on a quest, and we are not leaving until we get an answer.
Well, we're on our own quest, which is to squeeze this just tight enough to make my eyes bulge out a little bit.
But not so tight that I die.
Last week, this real scary ghost came down here looking for it.
It had black hair, but you could see through his skin.
It didn't like me, but that's just 'cause I got a soul of a ghostbuster.
Yeah, it said something about how I was worried Brett was gonna mug it.
Okay, so we're looking for a racist ghost with black hair who likes shoeshines.
I think I have the answer.
So much has changed around here.
I just wanted to remember the good old days when a shoeshine was two bits and there were no Mexicans in the music business.
If you don't mind, Councilman Milton, we just need to search this stamp.
I hate people, but you are okay.
If it makes you feel any better.
I had a big crush on you, too.
It does make me feel a little better.
So, I guess we are celebrating that you trusted me and I let you down.
I change my house locks every 16 days.
That key has been useless since the second Tuesday after I gave it to you.
What matters is that I trust you and admire you as a person.
I will be sorry to see you leave this town for many reasons.
Not the least of which is that you created a puzzle that even I couldn't solve.
And boy, oh boy, did you love Andy.
I totally know where the key is.
Because this tree reminds me of you.
And always here when you need it.
I have always felt a certain kinship with April, and this is proof that I was correct.
Not the nice things she said about me.
The fact that I buried a large amount of gold under that same tree years ago.
